text:
RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 35

All-male panels are common enough that composition alone proves little — plenty appoint women, and plenty of mixed panels discriminate. On its own it's context, not evidence.

Your stronger facts are the credentials gap (master's, licence, 12 years of directly relevant practice versus a bachelor's and consultation experience) and the ignored request for written reasons, which many public bodies are obliged to provide.

So: chase the written explanation in writing, citing any applicable policy or deadline. Ask for the scoring matrix and panel notes. Frame your query around how the criteria were weighted.

Mention the panel composition only as supporting context once you see the reasons. Leading with it invites dismissal; the qualifications comparison does not.
